1KI.P.1.28-31.text: David Renews His Oath to Bathsheba

1KI.P.13.11-34.text: The Old Prophet and the Man of God

1KI.P.16.29-34.text: Ahab Reigns in Israel, Marries Jezebel

1KI.P.19.9-18.text: The LORD Speaks to Elijah at Horeb

1KI.1.1-2.text: David’s servants want a young woman to care for him

1KI.1.3-4.text: Servants find Abishag to care for King David

1KI.1.5-6.text: Adonijah says he will be king

1KI.1.7-8.text: Joab and Abiathar support Adonijah; others do not

1KI.1.9-10.text: Adonijah holds a feast and does not invite Solomon

1KI.1.11-12.text: Nathan warns Bathsheba to save her life and Solomon’s

1KI.1.13-14.text: Nathan tells Bathsheba what to say to King David

1KI.1.15-17.text: Bathsheba reminds David of his promise about Solomon

1KI.1.18-19.text: Bathsheba tells David that Adonijah has become king

1KI.1.20-21.text: Bathsheba asks David to name the next king

1KI.1.22-23.text: Nathan the prophet arrives to see King David

1KI.1.24-25.text: Nathan asks David if he chose Adonijah as king

1KI.1.26-27.text: Nathan asks David who should sit on the throne

1KI.1.28-31.text: David Renews His Oath to Bathsheba

1KI.1.32-34.text: David orders that Solomon be anointed king at Gihon

1KI.1.35-37.text: David makes Solomon ruler and Benaiah agrees

1KI.1.38-40.text: Solomon is anointed king and the people rejoice

1KI.1.41-42.text: Adonijah and Joab hear the noise of the city

1KI.1.43-45.text: Jonathan tells Adonijah that Solomon is now king

1KI.1.46-48.text: Jonathan says Solomon sits on the throne

1KI.1.49-51.text: Adonijah’s guests flee and Adonijah fears Solomon

1KI.1.52-53.text: Solomon spares Adonijah and sends him home

1KI.2.1-4.text: David tells Solomon to be strong and obey the LORD

1KI.2.5-6.text: David tells Solomon to punish Joab for killing two men

1KI.2.7-7.text: David asks Solomon to be kind to Barzillai’s sons

1KI.2.8-9.text: David tells Solomon to deal with Shimei

1KI.2.13-15.text: Adonijah comes to Bathsheba to ask a favor

1KI.2.16-18.text: Adonijah asks Bathsheba to request Abishag for him

1KI.2.19-21.text: Bathsheba asks Solomon to give Abishag to Adonijah

1KI.2.22-23.text: Solomon swears that Adonijah must die for his request

1KI.2.24-25.text: Solomon sends Benaiah to kill Adonijah

1KI.2.26-27.text: Solomon removes Abiathar from the priesthood

1KI.2.28-29.text: Joab flees to the altar and Solomon sends Benaiah

1KI.2.30-31.text: Joab refuses to leave and Solomon orders his death

1KI.2.32-33.text: Solomon says Joab must pay for killing Abner and Amasa

1KI.2.34-35.text: Benaiah kills Joab and takes his place over the army

1KI.2.36-38.text: Solomon orders Shimei to live in Jerusalem and not leave

1KI.2.39-40.text: Shimei goes to Gath to bring back his runaway slaves

1KI.2.41-42.text: Solomon asks Shimei why he left Jerusalem

1KI.2.43-44.text: Solomon says Shimei broke his oath and did evil to David

1KI.2.45-46.text: Solomon has Benaiah kill Shimei, and the kingdom is secure

1KI.3.1-3.text: Solomon marries Pharaoh’s daughter and sacrifices at high places

1KI.3.4-5.text: God appears to Solomon at Gibeon and tells him to ask

1KI.3.6-6.text: Solomon thanks God for his faithfulness to David

1KI.3.7-9.text: Solomon asks God for an understanding heart to judge the people

1KI.3.10-12.text: God is pleased and gives Solomon a wise heart

1KI.3.13-14.text: God also promises Solomon riches, honor and long life

1KI.3.15-15.text: Solomon wakes, offers sacrifices in Jerusalem and holds a feast

1KI.3.16-17.text: Two women come to King Solomon, and one tells her story

1KI.3.18-20.text: The first woman says the other woman took her living son

1KI.3.21-22.text: The two women argue before Solomon about the living baby

1KI.3.23-25.text: Solomon orders the living child to be cut in two

1KI.3.26-28.text: Solomon gives the baby to its mother, and Israel honors him

1KI.4.1-4.text: The names of Solomon’s chief officials

1KI.4.5-6.text: More names of Solomon’s officials and their duties

1KI.4.7-10.text: Solomon’s twelve governors provide food for the king

1KI.4.11-14.text: The names of more governors and the places they rule

1KI.4.15-17.text: Three more governors, and two marry Solomon’s daughters

1KI.4.18-19.text: The last governors, including one in Judah

1KI.4.20-23.text: The people are happy, and Solomon rules many kingdoms

1KI.4.24-25.text: Solomon rules in peace, and the people live safely

1KI.4.26-28.text: Solomon’s horses, and the governors supply food each month

1KI.4.29-31.text: God gives Solomon great wisdom, and his fame spreads

1KI.4.32-34.text: Solomon speaks proverbs and songs, and people come to listen

1KI.5.1-3.text: Hiram sends envoys, and Solomon explains why David did not build

1KI.5.4-5.text: Solomon tells Hiram he plans to build the Lord’s house

1KI.5.6-6.text: Solomon asks Hiram to have cedars cut in Lebanon

1KI.5.7-8.text: Hiram rejoices and agrees to send cedar and cypress

1KI.5.9-9.text: Hiram will float the logs by sea if Solomon sends food

1KI.5.10-12.text: Hiram and Solomon exchange timber for food and make a treaty

1KI.5.13-14.text: Solomon sends 30,000 forced workers to Lebanon in shifts

1KI.5.15-16.text: Solomon had many workers and foremen

1KI.5.17-18.text: Builders cut large stones for the temple foundation

1KI.6.1-2.text: Solomon begins to build the LORD’s temple

1KI.6.3-4.text: Solomon builds the temple porch and windows

1KI.6.5-6.text: Solomon builds side rooms around the temple

1KI.6.7-8.text: The temple is built with stones cut at the quarry

1KI.6.9-10.text: Solomon finishes the temple roof and side rooms

1KI.6.14-15.text: Solomon lines the temple walls with cedar

1KI.6.16-18.text: Solomon makes the Most Holy Place inside the temple

1KI.6.19-20.text: Solomon prepares the inner room for the ark

1KI.6.21-22.text: Solomon covers the temple interior with gold

1KI.6.23-26.text: Solomon makes two large cherubim of olive wood

1KI.6.27-28.text: Solomon places the gold cherubim in the inner room

1KI.6.29-30.text: Solomon carves the walls and covers the floor with gold

1KI.6.31-32.text: Solomon makes carved olive wood doors for the inner room

1KI.6.33-35.text: Solomon makes carved doors for the temple entrance

1KI.6.37-38.text: Solomon finishes the temple in seven years

1KI.7.1-2.text: Solomon builds the House of the Forest of Lebanon

1KI.7.3-5.text: The House of the Forest has cedar roof and windows

1KI.7.6-6.text: Solomon builds a colonnade with a portico

1KI.7.7-7.text: Solomon builds the Hall of Justice for judging

1KI.7.8-8.text: Solomon builds houses for himself and Pharaoh’s daughter

1KI.7.9-10.text: Solomon uses large costly stones for the buildings

1KI.7.11-12.text: Stones and cedar beams are used for the courtyards

1KI.7.13-14.text: Solomon brings Huram, a skilled bronze worker, from Tyre

1KI.7.15-17.text: Huram casts two bronze pillars with capitals

1KI.7.18-19.text: Huram decorates the capitals with pomegranates and lilies

1KI.7.20-22.text: Huram sets up the pillars Jachin and Boaz

1KI.7.23-24.text: Huram makes the large bronze Sea

1KI.7.25-26.text: The Sea stands on twelve bronze oxen

1KI.7.27-29.text: Huram makes ten movable bronze stands

1KI.7.30-31.text: The stands have bronze wheels, axles, and basins

1KI.7.32-33.text: The stand wheels are made like chariot wheels

1KI.7.34-35.text: Each stand has four handles and a circular band

1KI.7.36-37.text: Huram engraves designs on the ten bronze stands

1KI.7.40-41.text: Huram finishes the pillars and other bronze work

1KI.7.42-43.text: The bronze pomegranates, stands and basins

1KI.7.44-45.text: The Sea, the twelve oxen and the bronze articles

1KI.7.46-47.text: Solomon casts the bronze articles and does not weigh them

1KI.7.48-49.text: Solomon makes the gold furnishings for the temple

1KI.7.50-50.text: Solomon makes gold basins, bowls and hinges

1KI.7.51-51.text: Solomon places David’s gifts in the temple treasuries

1KI.8.1-2.text: Solomon gathers Israel’s leaders to move the ark

1KI.8.3-5.text: The priests carry the ark up and Israel offers sacrifices

1KI.8.6-8.text: The priests place the ark in the Most Holy Place

1KI.8.9-11.text: The cloud of the LORD’s glory fills the temple

1KI.8.12-13.text: Solomon says he has built a house for the LORD

1KI.8.14-16.text: Solomon blesses Israel and praises the LORD’s promise

1KI.8.17-19.text: Solomon says David’s son will build the temple

1KI.8.20-21.text: Solomon says the LORD has kept his promise

1KI.8.22-24.text: Solomon praises the LORD for keeping his promise to David

1KI.8.25-26.text: Solomon asks the LORD to keep his promise to David

1KI.8.27-28.text: Solomon asks the LORD to hear his prayer

1KI.8.29-30.text: Solomon asks the LORD to hear prayers toward the temple

1KI.8.31-32.text: Solomon prays about a man who must take an oath

1KI.8.33-34.text: Solomon prays for Israel when enemies defeat them

1KI.8.35-36.text: Solomon prays for Israel when there is no rain

1KI.8.37-38.text: Solomon prays for Israel in famine, plague and siege

1KI.8.39-40.text: Solomon asks the LORD to forgive and repay each person

1KI.8.41-43.text: Solomon prays for foreigners who pray toward the temple

1KI.8.44-45.text: Solomon prays for Israel when the people go to war

1KI.8.46-47.text: Solomon prays for Israel when captives repent

1KI.8.48-48.text: Solomon prays for captives who return to the LORD

1KI.8.49-50.text: Solomon asks the LORD to forgive and show mercy

1KI.8.51-53.text: Solomon reminds the LORD that Israel is his people

1KI.8.54-56.text: Solomon blesses Israel and praises the LORD’s promises

1KI.8.57-58.text: Solomon asks the LORD to be with Israel and guide them

1KI.8.59-61.text: Solomon urges Israel to be fully devoted to the LORD

1KI.8.62-63.text: Solomon and Israel offer sacrifices to dedicate the temple

1KI.8.64-64.text: Solomon offers sacrifices in the courtyard of the temple

1KI.8.65-66.text: Solomon and Israel keep a feast for fourteen days

1KI.9.1-2.text: The LORD appears to Solomon a second time

1KI.9.3-3.text: The LORD says he has made the temple holy forever

1KI.9.4-5.text: The LORD promises Solomon a lasting throne if he obeys

1KI.9.6-7.text: The LORD warns that Israel will lose the land if it worships other gods

1KI.9.8-9.text: The LORD says people will see why the temple was ruined

1KI.9.10-11.text: Solomon gives twenty towns to Hiram king of Tyre

1KI.9.12-14.text: Hiram is not pleased with the towns Solomon gave him

1KI.9.15-16.text: Solomon uses forced labor to build many places

1KI.9.17-19.text: Solomon rebuilds Gezer and other cities

1KI.9.20-21.text: Solomon makes the people left in the land forced laborers

1KI.9.22-22.text: Solomon does not make any Israelites slaves

1KI.9.23-23.text: Solomon has 550 supervisors over the workers

1KI.9.24-24.text: Solomon builds the terraces after his wife moves to her palace

1KI.9.25-25.text: Solomon offers sacrifices three times a year and finishes the temple

1KI.9.26-28.text: Solomon builds a fleet and brings gold from Ophir

1KI.10.1-2.text: The queen of Sheba comes to Jerusalem to test Solomon

1KI.10.3-5.text: Solomon answers her questions and she is amazed

1KI.10.6-7.text: The queen of Sheba says Solomon is greater than the report

1KI.10.8-9.text: The queen of Sheba praises the LORD for making Solomon king

1KI.10.10-10.text: The queen of Sheba gives Solomon gold, spices and jewels

1KI.10.11-12.text: Hiram’s fleet brings almug wood and jewels from Ophir

1KI.10.13-13.text: Solomon gives the queen of Sheba gifts and she goes home

1KI.10.14-15.text: Solomon receives a great weight of gold each year

1KI.10.16-17.text: Solomon makes gold shields for the House of the Forest

1KI.10.18-20.text: Solomon makes a great throne of ivory and gold

1KI.10.21-22.text: Solomon’s cups and utensils are gold, and ships bring riches

1KI.10.23-25.text: Solomon is greater than all kings, and visitors bring gifts

1KI.10.26-27.text: Solomon gathers chariots and horses and makes silver common

1KI.10.28-29.text: Solomon’s men buy horses and chariots and sell them

1KI.11.1-2.text: Solomon loves many foreign women the LORD had forbidden

1KI.11.3-4.text: Solomon’s many wives turn his heart to other gods

1KI.11.5-6.text: Solomon follows other gods and does evil

1KI.11.7-8.text: Solomon builds high places for the gods of his wives

1KI.11.9-10.text: The LORD is angry with Solomon for following other gods

1KI.11.11-13.text: God tells Solomon he will take the kingdom from Solomon’s son

1KI.11.14-17.text: God raises up Hadad the Edomite against Solomon

1KI.11.18-19.text: Hadad goes to Egypt and marries the queen’s sister

1KI.11.20-22.text: Hadad asks Pharaoh to let him return to Edom

1KI.11.26-27.text: Jeroboam, Solomon’s servant, rebels against the king

1KI.11.28-30.text: Ahijah tears a new cloak into twelve pieces

1KI.11.31-33.text: Ahijah tells Jeroboam he will rule ten tribes

1KI.11.34-36.text: God will leave one tribe to Solomon’s son for David

1KI.11.37-39.text: God promises Jeroboam a lasting dynasty if he obeys

1KI.11.40-40.text: Solomon tries to kill Jeroboam, who flees to Egypt

1KI.12.1-2.text: Rehoboam goes to Shechem to be made king

1KI.12.3-5.text: The people ask Rehoboam to lighten their heavy work

1KI.12.6-7.text: The elders advise Rehoboam to serve the people kindly

1KI.12.8-9.text: Rehoboam rejects the elders and asks the young men

1KI.12.10-11.text: The young men advise Rehoboam to answer harshly

1KI.12.15-15.text: Rehoboam’s refusal fulfills the LORD’s word to Jeroboam

1KI.12.16-17.text: The Israelites reject David’s house and go home

1KI.12.18-19.text: Israel stones Adoram and Rehoboam flees to Jerusalem

1KI.12.20-20.text: Israel makes Jeroboam king; only Judah follows David’s house

1KI.12.21-21.text: Rehoboam gathers 180,000 warriors to fight Israel

1KI.12.22-24.text: God tells Rehoboam’s men not to fight, and they go home

1KI.12.25-27.text: Jeroboam fears the people will return to Rehoboam

1KI.12.28-30.text: Jeroboam makes two golden calves for the people to worship

1KI.12.31-32.text: Jeroboam appoints non-Levite priests and a feast

1KI.12.33-33.text: Jeroboam offers sacrifices at the altar in Bethel

1KI.13.1-3.text: A man of God speaks against the altar at Bethel

1KI.13.4-5.text: Jeroboam’s hand withers and the altar splits apart

1KI.13.6-7.text: The man of God prays and the king’s hand is healed

1KI.13.8-10.text: The man of God refuses the king’s offer and leaves

1KI.13.11-13.text: An old prophet in Bethel goes after the man of God

1KI.13.14-17.text: The old prophet asks the man of God to eat with him

1KI.13.18-19.text: The old prophet lies, and the man of God goes with him

1KI.13.20-22.text: God tells the man of God he will not reach his tomb

1KI.13.23-25.text: A lion kills the man of God on the road

1KI.13.26-28.text: The old prophet finds the body beside the lion

1KI.13.29-30.text: The old prophet buries the man of God in his tomb

1KI.13.31-32.text: The old prophet asks to be buried by the man of God

1KI.13.33-34.text: Jeroboam keeps appointing priests for the high places

1KI.14.1-3.text: Jeroboam sends his wife to ask Ahijah about his sick son

1KI.14.4-5.text: God warns old Ahijah that Jeroboam’s wife is coming

1KI.14.6-8.text: Ahijah says Jeroboam was not like David

1KI.14.9-10.text: God will bring disaster on Jeroboam’s family

1KI.14.11-13.text: Ahijah says Jeroboam’s son will die and be buried

1KI.14.14-16.text: God will punish Israel for Jeroboam’s sins

1KI.14.17-18.text: Jeroboam’s son dies as Ahijah said

1KI.14.21-22.text: Rehoboam rules Judah, and Judah does evil

1KI.14.23-24.text: Judah builds high places and copies evil customs

1KI.14.25-26.text: King Shishak of Egypt takes treasures from Jerusalem

1KI.14.27-28.text: Rehoboam makes bronze shields to replace the gold ones

1KI.14.29-31.text: Rehoboam dies and his son Abijam becomes king

1KI.15.1-3.text: Abijam becomes king of Judah and sins like his father

1KI.15.4-6.text: God keeps David’s family on the throne in Jerusalem

1KI.15.7-8.text: Abijam dies and his son Asa becomes king

1KI.15.9-11.text: Asa becomes king of Judah and does what is right

1KI.15.12-13.text: Asa removes idols and his grandmother’s Asherah pole

1KI.15.14-15.text: Asa serves the LORD fully and brings gifts to the temple

1KI.15.16-17.text: Baasha of Israel fortifies Ramah against Judah

1KI.15.18-19.text: Asa sends silver and gold to Ben-hadad for help

1KI.15.20-22.text: Ben-hadad attacks Israel, and Asa takes Ramah’s stones

1KI.15.25-26.text: Nadab becomes king of Israel and does evil

1KI.15.27-28.text: Baasha kills Nadab and becomes king

1KI.15.29-30.text: Baasha kills all Jeroboam’s family, as God said

1KI.15.31-32.text: War continues between Asa and Baasha

1KI.16.1-2.text: God accuses Baasha through Jehu of sin

1KI.16.3-4.text: God says he will destroy Baasha and his family

1KI.16.5-6.text: Baasha dies and his son Elah becomes king

1KI.16.7-7.text: God’s word through Jehu explains why Baasha is punished

1KI.16.8-10.text: Zimri kills King Elah and becomes king

1KI.16.11-13.text: Zimri kills all of Baasha’s family

1KI.16.14-14.text: The rest of Elah’s acts are in the royal records

1KI.16.15-17.text: Zimri reigns seven days; Israel makes Omri king

1KI.16.18-20.text: Zimri burns the palace down and dies in it

1KI.16.21-22.text: Israel is divided, and Omri defeats Tibni

1KI.16.23-24.text: Omri becomes king and builds the city of Samaria

1KI.16.25-26.text: Omri does more evil than all kings before him

1KI.16.27-28.text: Omri dies and his son Ahab becomes king

1KI.16.29-30.text: Ahab becomes king and does great evil

1KI.16.31-33.text: Ahab marries Jezebel and worships Baal

1KI.16.34-34.text: Hiel rebuilds Jericho and his sons die

1KI.17.1-1.text: Elijah tells Ahab that no rain will fall

1KI.17.2-4.text: God tells Elijah to hide by the Brook of Cherith

1KI.17.5-7.text: Ravens feed Elijah until the brook dries up

1KI.17.8-10.text: God sends Elijah to a widow in Zarephath

1KI.17.11-13.text: Elijah asks the widow to make him bread first

1KI.17.14-16.text: The widow’s flour and oil do not run out

1KI.17.17-18.text: The widow’s son dies and she blames Elijah

1KI.17.19-21.text: Elijah prays that the boy will live again

1KI.17.22-24.text: God restores the boy’s life, and the widow believes

1KI.18.1-2.text: God sends Elijah to Ahab in the third year of drought

1KI.18.3-4.text: Ahab calls Obadiah, who hid the LORD’s prophets

1KI.18.5-6.text: Ahab and Obadiah search the land for grass

1KI.18.7-8.text: Elijah meets Obadiah and tells him to call Ahab

1KI.18.9-11.text: Obadiah fears Ahab will kill him for finding Elijah

1KI.18.12-13.text: Obadiah says he has served the LORD and hid prophets

1KI.18.14-15.text: Elijah promises Obadiah to meet Ahab today

1KI.18.16-17.text: Ahab meets Elijah and calls him a troubler

1KI.18.18-19.text: Elijah tells Ahab to gather Israel and the prophets

1KI.18.20-21.text: Elijah asks the people to choose the LORD or Baal

1KI.18.22-24.text: Elijah proposes a test: the God who answers by fire

1KI.18.25-26.text: The prophets of Baal call on Baal, but no one answers

1KI.18.27-29.text: Elijah mocks Baal’s prophets, but there is no answer

1KI.18.30-32.text: Elijah repairs the altar of the LORD with twelve stones

1KI.18.33-35.text: Elijah has water poured on the offering and wood

1KI.18.36-37.text: Elijah prays that the people will know the LORD is God

1KI.18.38-40.text: Fire from the LORD falls and Baal’s prophets are killed

1KI.18.41-42.text: Elijah tells Ahab rain is coming, then bows on Carmel

1KI.18.43-44.text: Elijah’s servant sees a small cloud over the sea

1KI.18.45-46.text: Heavy rain falls and Elijah runs ahead of Ahab

1KI.19.1-3.text: Jezebel threatens Elijah, and he runs away in fear

1KI.19.4-6.text: Elijah asks to die, and an angel gives him food

1KI.19.7-8.text: Elijah eats and walks forty days to Horeb

1KI.19.9-10.text: Elijah tells the LORD he is the only prophet left

1KI.19.11-12.text: The LORD comes to Elijah in a still, small voice

1KI.19.13-14.text: Elijah again says he is the only prophet left

1KI.19.15-16.text: The LORD tells Elijah to anoint Hazael, Jehu and Elisha

1KI.19.17-18.text: Seven thousand in Israel have not bowed to Baal

1KI.19.19-20.text: Elijah throws his cloak around Elisha

1KI.19.21-21.text: Elisha cooks his oxen and follows Elijah

1KI.20.1-3.text: Ben-hadad besieges Samaria and demands Ahab’s wealth

1KI.20.4-6.text: Ben-hadad says he will search Ahab’s palace tomorrow

1KI.20.7-8.text: The elders tell Ahab not to accept Ben-hadad’s terms

1KI.20.9-10.text: Ahab refuses, and Ben-hadad threatens Samaria again

1KI.20.11-12.text: Ahab tells Ben-hadad not to boast too soon

1KI.20.13-15.text: A prophet tells Ahab the LORD will give him victory

1KI.20.16-17.text: Ahab’s men march out while Ben-hadad is drinking

1KI.20.18-19.text: Ben-hadad orders his men to take the Israelites alive

1KI.20.20-21.text: Israel defeats the Arameans, and Ben-hadad escapes

1KI.20.22-23.text: A prophet warns Ahab that Aram will attack in spring

1KI.20.24-25.text: Ben-hadad plans a new army to fight on the plain

1KI.20.26-27.text: Aram and Israel gather for battle at Aphek

1KI.20.28-28.text: A man of God promises Ahab victory over the Arameans

1KI.20.29-30.text: Israel kills many Arameans, and Ben-hadad hides

1KI.20.31-32.text: Ben-hadad’s servants beg Ahab for mercy

1KI.20.33-34.text: Ahab makes a treaty with Ben-hadad and lets him go

1KI.20.35-36.text: A man refuses to strike a prophet and a lion kills him

1KI.20.37-38.text: Another man strikes the prophet, who disguises himself

1KI.20.39-40.text: The prophet tells Ahab a story about a lost prisoner

1KI.20.41-43.text: The prophet tells Ahab he will lose his life

1KI.21.1-2.text: Ahab asks Naboth for his vineyard

1KI.21.3-4.text: Naboth refuses, and Ahab is sullen and angry

1KI.21.5-7.text: Jezebel tells Ahab she will get the vineyard

1KI.21.8-10.text: Jezebel writes letters to have Naboth killed

1KI.21.11-14.text: The elders do as Jezebel says and Naboth is killed

1KI.21.15-16.text: Ahab takes Naboth’s vineyard after Naboth dies

1KI.21.17-18.text: The LORD sends Elijah to meet Ahab in the vineyard

1KI.21.19-20.text: Elijah says Ahab murdered Naboth and will die

1KI.21.21-22.text: The LORD will end Ahab’s family because of his sin

1KI.21.23-24.text: The LORD says dogs will eat Jezebel and Ahab’s people

1KI.21.25-26.text: Ahab did great evil, urged on by Jezebel

1KI.21.27-29.text: Ahab humbles himself, and the LORD delays the disaster

1KI.22.1-2.text: Jehoshaphat visits Ahab after three years of peace

1KI.22.3-4.text: Ahab asks Jehoshaphat to fight for Ramoth-gilead

1KI.22.5-6.text: Ahab’s 400 prophets say he should go to war

1KI.22.7-9.text: Jehoshaphat asks for a prophet; Ahab names Micaiah

1KI.22.10-12.text: Zedekiah and the prophets say Ahab will win

1KI.22.13-15.text: Micaiah answers Ahab as the other prophets did

1KI.22.16-17.text: Micaiah sees Israel scattered like sheep

1KI.22.18-20.text: Micaiah sees the LORD asking who will entice Ahab

1KI.22.21-23.text: Micaiah says a lying spirit is in Ahab’s prophets

1KI.22.24-25.text: Zedekiah strikes Micaiah in the face

1KI.22.26-28.text: Ahab jails Micaiah, who says Ahab will not return

1KI.22.29-30.text: Ahab disguises himself for the battle

1KI.22.31-33.text: The Aramean commanders chase Jehoshaphat by mistake

1KI.22.34-34.text: A man shoots an arrow and wounds Ahab

1KI.22.35-36.text: Ahab dies in his chariot that evening

1KI.22.37-38.text: Ahab is buried, and dogs lick his blood

1KI.22.39-40.text: Ahab’s reign ends and his son Ahaziah becomes king

1KI.22.43-44.text: Jehoshaphat does right but high places remain

1KI.22.45-47.text: Jehoshaphat removes shrine prostitutes from the land

1KI.22.48-50.text: Jehoshaphat’s ships are wrecked, and he dies
